gen-dafont-woodgod-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk draws each glyph as a steady ribbon, like a technical pen, with counters that stay open. Woodgod sits above it with a vintage, commanding voice and tall lowercase that nearly touches its capitals, which makes the sans below feel measured.
gen-eater-fs-amulya: Eater looks dark and aggressive, with thin strokes beside weightier stems and wide gaps between letters. Amulya follows in a plain sans that keeps its curves generous, so a longer page of text goes down smoothly and modern.
gen-eater-fs-chillax: Menacing and jagged, Eater spaces its letters wide and keeps its ascenders short. And Chillax runs a loose, spaghetti-like line through a plain sans body, so a longer read feels casual and unhurried.
gen-eater-fs-plein: Dark, spiky and wide-spaced, Eater hits hard. Plein takes over in sans-serif with a clear channel into each round letter, so a long passage feels reliable, clean and easy on the eye.
gen-eater-fs-roundo: Roundo reads smooth and geometric, with an n whose arch matches its stem and small counters that never clog. But Eater, with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones, brings the gritty edge that the plain sans lets stand alone.
gen-eater-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads open and friendly, its curves pulled well off the stems. Eater, dark and aggressive with its short ascenders, takes the headline spot while the sans keeps everything underneath approachable and level.
gen-eater-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve, quietly dependable. Eater's crossbars run slightly thinner than its stems, so a plain sans body keeps a long read easy.
gen-eater-gf-aclonica: Eater's wide-spaced, hairline-free strokes feel dark and aggressive. Aclonica stretches out in sans-serif with a deep midsection and a thickness shift you sense more than see, so longer text moves along in a long, loose line.
gen-eater-gf-allerta: Professional and plain-spoken, Allerta sets wide, loose letters with a prominent x-height. Eater brings a soft contrast with dark, aggressive stems, and next to the sans it feels like a growl over a clear voice.
gen-eater-gf-alumni-sans: Alumni Sans reads clean and approachable, ascenders barely clearing its x-height. Eater is best at dark, aggressive impact with wide gaps, while the plain sans is best at staying open and understated with its pulled-apart curves.
